tagline.text: A wildlife sanctuary island in southern Negros that protects five lagoons and bat caves

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: Generally December–May (check sea conditions before visiting)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,650–5,000 (per person, island package rates; flights and overland transport to the pier not included)

children.text: Danjugan Island is a 43-hectare wildlife and marine sanctuary off Bulata in Cauayan, southern Negros. A foundation manages its five lagoons, bat caves, mangrove forest and coral reefs, and you can visit on a reservation-only day trip or an overnight camp stay.
Danjugan Island is a small island off the barangay of Bulata in Cauayan, Negros Occidental. It covers about
43 hectares
and is roughly
1.5km
long and
0.5km

wide, so it is easy to explore on foot. Unlike a typical resort island, it is run as a wildlife and marine sanctuary. The island has five lagoons, bat caves, limestone and mangrove forests and beach forest, and seagrass beds and coral reefs surround it. Less than 10 percent of the island is developed, and the rest is left to wildlife.

The island's story goes back to 1994. According to its official introduction, Danjugan was once threatened by overfishing and damage, and it was a pair of white-bellied sea eagles nesting in the island's tallest tree that changed its fate. When the previous owner offered to sell that single tree, the founders of the Philippine Reef and Rainforest Conservation Foundation (PRRCFI) offered to buy the whole island instead, and so the island was saved. The foundation still owns and manages it, and for years it was used as a nature classroom, for research and for educational camps before tourism began.

Danjugan promotes a low-impact, low-volume ecotourism model in which a small number of visitors get a lot of value. The fees you pay include a conservation fee that supports island operations, the livelihoods of the Bulata residents who protect the island, environmental education and community development. The island introduces visitors to the tabon (Philippine scrubfowl), a type of megapode, as well as fireflies, Geoffroy's rousette bats and sea turtles that come to nest. That makes it less an island for pretty photos and more an island for learning by walking through forest and sea. The linked Danjugan Island Nature Tourism Program is described as supporting work to protect species and habitats in Danjugan and southern Negros, livelihoods for the Bulata community, marine and wildlife camps for public schools, mentoring of scholars in fisheries, agriculture and forestry, and trainings and workshops. The fact that your visit directly supports conservation is a big reason to choose Danjugan.

All visits require an official reservation, and there are four kinds of visit: the three-hour "Discover Danjugan" tour, a day trip, and two overnight camps. It is close to Sipalay in southwestern Negros, so it pairs well with a Sipalay itinerary, but because it takes several hours overland from Bacolod, give yourself plenty of travel time. It lies in waters toward the Panay Gulf and the Sulu Sea, and the town of Cauayan and the Bulata coast are described as a recently growing tourism area thanks to white sand beaches and marine and wildlife diversity. Every year on January 25, Cauayan holds the Lubay-lubay Festival and the Feast of the Conversion of St. Paul.

The island has five lagoons. The official introduction does not name each one, but the name of the Moray Lagoon camp shows how central lagoons are to the island. You explore them with a guide by snorkeling or kayaking.

blocks.title: Bat caves and Geoffroy's rousette bats

children.text: The island has bat caves and is described as home to Geoffroy's rousette bats. The caves are wildlife habitat, so follow your guide's instructions and keep quiet.

Limestone forest, mangrove forest and beach forest are gathered on a single island. The tours include trekking and birdwatching, and you can learn about the tabon (Philippine scrubfowl) and fireflies.
The official site says sea turtles nest on the island and that its protection work safeguards sea turtle nests. Ask when you book about the nesting season and whether you can see them.

blocks.title: Snorkeling in reefs and seagrass beds

children.text: You snorkel and skin dive in the coral reefs and wide seagrass beds around the island. Gear is included in every package, and a guide accompanies you.

blocks.title: Typhoon Beach and Moray Lagoon camps

children.text: To stay overnight, choose the Typhoon Beach Camp with private rooms or the Moray Lagoon Camp with open-air eco-cabanas. There is no air conditioning or TV; it is a stay for spending the night in nature.

The island sponsors marine and wildlife camps for public school students, and it also opened registration for its 2026 camps. If you are interested in nature education, check the camp news on the official site first.
Board the boat at Antol Danjugan Port in Bulata. If you are late you must arrange a separate boat yourself, so arrive early.

Have lunch and snacks, then continue with activities such as snorkeling or kayaking.

The day trip lasts up to 8 hours including transfers, from 08:30 to 16:30.
Overnight guests board the boat at the pier at noon, go to the island and check in.
Join the guided activities (snorkeling, skin diving, kayaking, trekking and birdwatching).
Have dinner at the camp and spend the night on the island. Loud noise and bonfires are prohibited.
Check out.

Danjugan is an island you reach by boat, so weather and sea conditions decide whether you can visit. The official booking guidelines say a visit may be canceled automatically if there is a Coast Guard advisory, a gale warning or a storm signal.
In general the dry season from December to May tends to have calmer seas, but I did not find monthly climate data for this area, so check the latest weather forecast before you book.

There are only two places to stay on the island. Typhoon Beach Camp has private rooms with private toilets and showers, and Moray Lagoon Camp has open-air eco-cabanas with individual mattresses and mosquito nets and shared toilets and showers. Neither has air conditioning or TV. Moray Lagoon Camp is said to get Smart, Dito and limited Globe signal. Fresh water and solar electricity are shared, so use them sparingly.

Meals are included in every package, and overnight packages include full-board meals, snacks, coffee and drinking water. Tell them about dietary requests when you book. On the mainland, Punta Bulata Resort in Bulata is described as having Department of Tourism AA accreditation, and beach accommodation on the Sipalay side is also nearby.
Apply first through the official booking form or the listed phone numbers and email. Assume you cannot enter without a reservation.
The boat leaves at a set time, and if you are more than 15 minutes late you must pay
and arrange a separate transfer yourself, so get to the pier early.
The boarding point can change with the tide and weather. Be sure to check the messages staff send you.
Cut down on single-use items, carry your trash out, and it is a good idea to bring a reusable bottle and reef-safe sunscreen.
Phone signal is weak, so save maps and your booking confirmation beforehand.
Tell them about allergies or dietary requests when you book.
There are no refunds. Instead, you can reschedule within 1 year, and payments can reportedly be transferred to another guest or a later booking.
Electricity and fresh water are shared on the island. Use them sparingly and keep showers short.
For inquiries, call +63 908 525 4108 or +63 917 320 1099, or email patrons@danjuganisland.ph. Contact details can change, so check the official site.
The island is a sanctuary, so bonfires, loud noise, invasive species and pets are all prohibited.
A Coast Guard advisory, gale warning or storm signal can cancel a visit automatically, so leave room in your travel schedule.
Canceling a booking does not get you a refund; only rescheduling is possible. Check the latest notice for the rules.
The island has bat caves and sea turtle nests, so do not approach caves or nests without your guide's instruction.
Overland travel is long, so a same-day transfer from Bacolod airport is tight. It is safer to spend the night nearby the day before.
Under its conservation policy, take nothing from the sea. Leave only photos behind.
